en: To deceive someone; or to understand and remember information; or to bring something inside; or to include something.
ex: He was taken in by the scam.
他被這個騙局矇騙了。

en: To increase in amount or level; or to be built; or to explode.
ex: Food prices have gone up again.
食品價格又上漲了。

en: To not turn off a light, machine or appliance; or to keep wearing something.
ex: Please don't leave the lights on when you go out.
外出時請不要讓燈開著。

en: To turn to face the opposite direction; or to improve a bad situation.
ex: She turned around when she heard her name.
她聽到自己的名字時轉過身來。

en: To leave a bus, train or plane; or to leave work; or to avoid punishment.
ex: We got off at the wrong station.
我們在錯誤的車站下車了。

en: To give something to each person in a group; or to pass something around.
ex: She handed around the cookies.
她把餅乾傳給大家。

en: To get rid of something or stop using it.
col: do away with the old system
ex: The school decided to do away with uniforms.
學校決定廢除制服。

en: To gain control or power over someone or something.
col: get the upper hand over rivals
ex: Our team finally got the upper hand.
我們隊終於占了上風。

en: To be enough for everyone; or to spread among people; or to move in a circle.
ex: There's enough pizza to go around.
披薩夠大家分。

en: To remain after the rest has been used or taken.
ex: There was a lot of food left over after the party.
派對後剩下很多食物。

en: To remove something you do not want; or to free yourself from something unpleasant.
ex: I can't get rid of this cough.
我擺脫不了這個咳嗽。

en: To allow someone or something to take the position of another.
ex: Old customs give place to new ones.
舊習俗讓位給新習俗。

en: To appear or become known; or (of flowers) to bloom; or to be published or released.
ex: The stars came out one by one.
星星一顆接一顆出現了。

en: To no longer be able to see someone or something; or to forget something important.
ex: We must not lose sight of our main goal.
我們不能忘了主要目標。

en: To move back or retreat; or to be less successful than before.
ex: The army had to fall back to the river.
軍隊不得不退到河邊。

en: To officially ask for something, such as a job or a payment.
ex: He put in for a transfer to another city.
他申請調到另一個城市。

en: To end a romantic relationship or friendship with someone.
ex: She broke up with him last month.
她上個月和他分手了。

en: To lift something from a surface; or to collect someone in a car; or to learn something without effort.
ex: I'll pick you up at the airport.
我會到機場接你。

en: To happen, especially in a way that is not planned; or (of a ship) to change direction.
ex: How did this situation come about?
這種局面是怎麼形成的？

en: To use up money quickly; or to read through something quickly; or to rehearse.
ex: Let's run through the plan once more.
我們再把計畫走一遍。

en: To cut something into small pieces; or to upset someone very much.
ex: Cut up the onions and add them to the pan.
把洋蔥切碎加進鍋裡。

en: To wear clothes or make-up; or to turn on a device; or to pretend; or to stage a show.
ex: Put on your coat; it's cold.
穿上外套，天氣很冷。

en: To put something in the place where it is kept; or to save money; or to put a person in prison.
ex: Please put away your books.
請把書收好。

en: Too difficult for someone to understand.
col: the lecture was above my head
ex: The math lecture was completely above my head.
那堂數學課我完全聽不懂。

en: To create space for someone or something by moving or removing things.
ex: Let's move the sofa to make room for the table.
把沙發移開，騰出位置放桌子。

en: To store something, such as money or food, for future use; or to be ill and unable to work.
ph: lay up for a rainy day
ex: Squirrels lay up nuts for the winter.
松鼠為冬天儲存堅果。

en: To continue doing something; or to continue at the same level; or to stay informed.
ex: Keep up the good work!
繼續保持好成績！

en: To read through something quickly; or to practice something; or to hit someone with a vehicle.
ex: Let's run over the main points again.
讓我們再複習一遍要點。

en: To amuse yourself with something; or to treat someone or something in a careless way.
ex: Don't play with my feelings.
不要玩弄我的感情。

en: To be unable to feel or respond to something; or to no longer exist for someone.
ex: He seemed lost to all sense of duty.
他似乎已全然喪失責任感。

en: To cause serious trouble or damage to someone or something.
ph: play the devil with one's health
col: play the devil with the schedule
ex: The storm played the devil with our plans.
暴風雨攪亂了我們的計畫。

en: To interrupt someone who is speaking; or to drive in front of another vehicle suddenly.
col: cut in front of a car
ex: Please don't cut in while I'm talking.
我說話時請不要打斷。

en: To become fainter, weaker or less noticeable, then stop.
ex: The music slowly died away.
音樂漸漸消失了。

en: To recover from an illness or an unhappy experience; or to cross to the other side of something.
ex: It took her a long time to get over the loss.
她花了很長的時間才走出失去親人的傷痛。

en: To meet with other people for a social purpose; or to bring things together.
ex: Let's get together next weekend.
我們下週末聚一聚吧。

en: To suddenly think of something; or to appear in your mind.
col: an idea came into my head
ex: A brilliant idea came into my head.
我腦中浮現一個絕妙的主意。

en: To try to find someone or something; or to hope for or expect something.
ex: I'm looking for my glasses.
我在找我的眼鏡。

en: To get to know someone by chance and become friendly with them.
ph: pick up with an old friend
col: pick up with someone at a bar
ex: He picked up with some students on the train.
他在火車上結識了幾位學生。

en: To walk carefully, choosing where to put your feet.
ex: She picked her way through the crowded market.
她在擁擠的市場中小心地前行。

en: To begin spending time with someone, especially someone considered unsuitable; or to start a relationship with someone.
ph: take up with the wrong crowd
col: take up with a new friend
ex: He took up with a bad crowd at school.
他在學校和一群壞朋友混在一起。
